truth.title: globally-installable-npm-package
truth.content: Truths is published as an npm package that can be installed globally. It exposes two bin scripts: "truths" (an umbrella CLI built with commander) and "truths-server" (a shortcut that launches the HTTP server).
truth.notes: The prebuilt frontend ships inside the package so no build step runs on the user's machine.

truth.title: frontend-react-vite
truth.content: The frontend is a React single-page app written in TypeScript and built with Vite. The build output goes to dist/, which the server serves as static assets.

truth.title: backend-express-server
truth.content: The backend is a JavaScript (ESM) Express server. It lists truths.xml / truths-*.xml files in the current folder and exposes a small JSON API to read and save them. It starts on port 3000 and advances to the next free port if busy.
truth.notes: Port selection uses the get-port package; the browser is opened automatically on start.

truth.title: truths-stored-as-xml
truth.content: Each truths file is XML: a root element wrapping a list of truth entries, each with a title, createdBy, approved, content, relatesTo, notes, and labels. The editor uses fast-xml-parser to round-trip between the XML and the structured form.

truth.title: linting-with-eslint-config-ironplate
truth.content: Code quality is enforced with ESLint using eslint-config-ironplate: the node.js preset for the backend JavaScript and the react-typescript preset for the frontend TypeScript, scoped by directory.

truth.title: content-hash-uses-cyrb53
truth.content: A truth's <contentHash> is a cyrb53 hash of its <content>, computed by a pure-JS function shared by the browser, the node scripts, and the migration. A JS implementation is used deliberately: crypto.subtle.digest is async, and like crypto.randomUUID it is unavailable over plain HTTP on a LAN address (the phone case), while Node's crypto.createHash is not in the browser. cyrb53 is deterministic and identical across all of them, rendered as zero-padded hex (~13 chars).
truth.notes: The hash is recomputed from content on load rather than read from the stored <contentHash>, so a hand-edited value is corrected on the next save.

truth.title: approval-tracks-content-staleness
truth.content: Human approval is stored as the content hash captured at sign-off time, kept in the <approved> field. A truth's approval state is derived by comparing that stored hash against the current content hash: 'none' when never approved, 'current' when they match, and 'stale' when the content changed since sign-off. Only 'current' truths count as approved; a stale approval drops out of the approved count until reapproved.
truth.notes: The derivation is a pure function, so the same logic backs both the editor's status filter and any other consumer.

truth.title: order-insensitive-git-diff-driver
truth.content: Truth XML files get a custom git diff driver (diff=truths-canon in .gitattributes) that runs node scripts/canonicalize-truths.js. Canonicalization sorts fields within a truth, sorts whole truth entries by title, and sorts relatesTo/labels items, so any pure reordering collapses to identical output and produces no diff. git refuses to let a repo commit a diff driver command, so the command lives in a committed .gitconfig fragment that the prepare script wires into .git/config via include.path.
truth.notes: The prepare-script bootstrap is guarded to a real checkout: installed as a registry dependency there is no .git, so it is a no-op.

truth.title: ai-generated-truths-via-headless-claude
truth.content: The backend can generate new truths on demand by spawning a headless "claude -p" agent with --dangerously-skip-permissions in the workspace folder. The agent is prompted to read the codebase and existing truths and append entries directly to the target file. A request is capped at 50 truths to guard against a runaway run, and the child process is killed after a 10-minute timeout.
truth.notes: The CLI's raw stdout is forwarded to the browser console for debugging; a missing claude binary surfaces as a "Claude CLI not found on PATH" error.

truth.title: truths-file-discovery-and-ignore
truth.content: The server discovers truth files by globbing **/truths*.xml under the workspace (excluding node_modules and .git), then filtering names through a validator and a .truthsignore file. The validator only accepts the basename truths.xml or truths-<something>.xml and rejects any ".."/"." path segment; combined with a defense-in-depth check that the resolved path stays inside cwd, a request can never traverse out of the workspace.
truth.notes: .truthsignore uses gitignore semantics and is re-read on every request, so edits take effect without a server restart, mirroring how git re-reads .gitignore.

truth.title: potentially-truncated-text-should-have-title-attribute
truth.content: In UI, potentially truncated text should have title attribute, so that the user can see the full value.

truth.title: add-files-from-explorer-view-in-left-panel
truth.content: It should be possible to add files from the left panel (explorer view)

truth.title: more-options-for-files-and-folders-in-explorer-view
truth.content:
In Explorer View on the left panel, for each folder/file, there should be a "More" menu icon and clicking upon that should show more options (like "Delete" and "New File..." (in case of directory)).
The "Delete" should show a warning first before deleting.
